In this game I have :
- stolen KFC's most secret recipe
- read Doom fanfiction
- accessed the computer of a major Naruto fan
- nearly been traced and sent to jail, working relentlessly to avert this under a time limit that slowly painted my screen red, while synthwave was blasting in the background

And many more, but I'm not gonna spoil it all. Super good game.

Pros :
- Sleek interface, easy to use
- Shiny effects and nice atmosphere
- Messing up and getting traced is one of the most intense experiences in recent gaming history
- Objectives are clear, you always know what you have to do even if the mission text doesn't always tell you
- 10/10 soundtrack
- Game uses a terminal, always gonna be a pro for me

Cons :
- Upon viewing certain programs and nodes the framerate will be locked at 30 and 20fps
- Bloom makes it hard to read text and if you deactivate it you lose practically nothing graphics-wise
- Kind of short. 6-7 hours for a first time completion, nice replayability though
- Bypassing proxies is an extremely tedious process, and they're commonplace
- Like Uplink a decade before Hacknet's release, it also tells you early that you have to delete logs so as to not get caught. However, unlike Uplink, if you do leave logs all over the place, absolutely nobody is going to trace you since apparently nobody's ever at their computer
- Hexclock and Notes take an outrageous amount of RAM
- Factions could've been better (Entropy and CSEC anyway), there is no incentive to keep doing missions for them once you have unlocked the story mission by going up the ranks since there is no money to be earned and the other hackers that have been here for way longer than you don't care one Bit (hehe) that they got owned by a script kiddie that entered the faction an hour ago
- [EDIT] I should also mention that the game is way too easy except for some nodes. For instance, if you're about to get traced but you have hacked every port, and then you disconnect and reconnect, the trace will be dropped and you'll be allowed to look at every file without any time constraint. Now, this isn't a con for most people, but it is for me because the moment you know about the point I just made plus the point about the logs, then the difficulty suddenly disappears, and the only moment your hacking skills will be challenged is at the very end of the game in a story mission.

All of these are more or less nitpicks though, the game is a solid 8/10. The team behind Hacknet has expressed a desire to make Hacknet 2, and honestly with Hacknet 1 as a base, I think they could easily create the best hacking game of all time.

Longer Review (if you just want a short to-the-point review, scroll down to the Short Review section):

When I was reading reviews before I purchased this game, I was looking for helpful, detailed accounts of gameplay, well-developed concept, and good gamer reaction. There are plenty of those reviews out there (which I recommend you read through), so I'm going to be brief.

I bought this on sale as the game/soundtrack bundle for $7.50--it was an absolute steal. This game is so well-put together it will make you think "now why aren't all games so carefully and caringly developed like this one?" Matt Trobbiani put in a ton, a TON of work into this game, and for any gamer who appreciates a challenge, puzzles, hacking, story, and other fun little tidbits, this is a 5/5 star game.

When going through negative reviews, I saw that many claimed the game introduced too much too soon. I disagree. As a puzzle lover, I may have had a leg up on the matter, but I had no hacking genre game experience prior to this game (and I have spent the last 15 hours playing it and completing it; and I loved it). The game does introduce a lot of coding concepts toward the beginning, it's true, but the key to this game ultimately is patience and the willingness to actually read EVERYTHING. A) This will benefit you, and help you play your way through the game, and B) there is a ton of extra content that you'll miss out on if you skip over everything.

Short Review: The game introduces enough at the beginning to make you actually think and struggle a little bit, but if you have patience and read the text, you'll get the hang of it in the middle and get into the groove of the game. And that's when Trobbiani throws the curveball at you in regard to both gameplay and storyline: everything gets so much more intense, and in the best way possible. On sale, this game is an absolute bargain but is definitely worth the full price tag. An ABSOLUTE MUST for hacker/puzzle genre lovers, and a RECOMMENDED playthrough for gamers who appreciate a highly innovative and well-developed/conceptualized game.

It's possible that HackNet is the most fun I've had in a LONG LONG time.    At first, I thought it was a little hokey.. Sort of like how Hollywood movies portray hacking.. And then as the plot develops (closer to the end), everything started to fit into place... The overdone interfaces, the limited options... everything...  slotted together... perfectly..

OK, so this game is pretty much for geeks and programming/unix nerds.  If you've never used a command prompt, and think typing your username into the PSN login is "programming", this ain't for you.   This game relies on an X-Server-like interface, and relies on fast typing, and a fair working knowledge of what a server is, ports, IP Addresses, and so on. Knowing that you can press "up" in a shell window to get to previously typed commands, for instance, can save a lot of typing.. It's that kind of knowledge which comes in handy...

The game presents itself as an X-server interface with a fixed layout (which can be modified in-game!), you just can't drag windows about. You wouldn't want to, anyway.  The layout is perfect for what you need.   There's a "net map" to show your progress, a terminal for typing in commands, and an all-purpose web-browser interface.

You have control of an advanced unix-based OS which has serious MIL-spec hacking software installed on it.  The server comes with an timed message, which asks you to perform 'a favour' for the previous owner of the software...  And from that point on, you're sucked headfirst into the screen, as you probe, hack, and trace your way around the internet.

You're not alone, though.  There's a few groups out there who do this sort of thing every day of the week.  Some of them are REALLY good.  But all of them are using old-gen kit, so while you know next-to-nothing, you're already as powerful as the best of them... With a little training, and some experience, you can be the best Hacker on the 'Net... 

The game is about 50% hacking simulation (a-la Hollywood) with flashy graphics, and fast, heart-pounding music to crank up the tension.   You have to 'connect' to a server to inject cracks and exploits onto it.  Once running, you can disconnect from the server and let them run.  As long as you're connected, you're vulnerable to being traced and back-hacked!   But if you disconnect too often or too quickly, you may need to start over.  It's a brilliant device which deviates slightly from accepted terminology, but works great as a game device.    The other 50% of the game is done after you've successfully breached a server.  Your OS filters out all the unnecessary stuff, leaving you with the important bits.. And buried in that dross are gold nuggets.. Usernames, passwords, blackmail material, recipes (sic), saved IRC quotes, and all-important IP addresses to other servers.  

Once you hook up with a team of other hackers, you can opt to take on 'contracts' to hack into servers to perform tasks.  Some of them require you to figure out where you have to hack, and might involve chain-hacks of three or four servers.  Each one holds the key (somewhere) to the next (you hope), or might be a dead-end to slow you down....  Who knows? The game randomizes some element each playthrough, so you may never be 100% sure!

As you get better, you may find your current group is pretty small-fry, or doesn't take the sorts of things you want to.. you may want to move up in the world....  But all the time, at the back of your mind... Who was the previous owner of this awesome system?  Am I the only one with it?  who else has it?  Why can I run Windows .EXEs on a *nix box?!?!    Perhaps you'll get to find out....

Partway through the game, there's a mini-easter egg which spawns a nice little side-plot.  You can continue on through without triggering it.. But once you win the game, there's a (sort-of) hint about how to trigger it.. but TBH, just go read the forums.    The side-plot is short, sweet, and switches things up a bit.

I loved the variety in the game.   It's amazing, because (at its core) everything is the same... A circle with an IP address, that exposes ports, and may be protected...  But how you get that circle varies... And what that circle entails varies...   The logs, emails, and text files throughout the game paint a glorious picture (with many spelling mistakes!),  giving you a grand idea of the people at the other end of the pipe.

From the first moment I started this game, I loved every second of it.  When I was away from the PC, I was trying to think   a) how I could solve the puzzle I was stuck at   and  b) how I could get back to the PC to play it...

In-game explanation is fair.  Actually figuring out what you have to do is relatively straightforward:  It generally boils down to executing a particular command to attempt to breach a particular piece of security.   The in-game explanation, however, makes it sound a little more complicated than it is.  Just read it through, and try the commands out.

Well, a fter a 9 hours journey in the world of virtual hacking, I must say I'm satisfied but also a bit sad it was so short. 

At first, I thought it would be a needlessly complicated and boring game but I decided to give it a chance and, boy did I make the right decision. The game was complex enough that anybody without basic computer skills wouldn't stand a chance against this game but it's simplified enough that you don't have to remember dozens of complex commands, you can easily complete a command by pressing TAB, which makes the games less of a chore.

The story is engaging as the death of a known hacker named Bit is slowly revealed to be not a fruit of some accident but something more sinister and you are his last hope of successfully executing plans that might be the difference between corporate digital control and freedom. Along the way, there are contracts to fulfill, ranging from simple information retrieval to adding or removing entries from a death row record and even hacking a suffering patient's pacemaker to give its host a peaceful, painless death. And as you progress, you'll find programs that will help you get inside more secure systems in order to complete the more difficult contracts.

The game is not devoid of humor as you'll find IRC chat logs and other documents inside the devices you hack and some of them are hilarious, such as a guy replacing the word "wand" with "wang" in the first Harry Potter book and has posted some excerpts that are good for a laugh or a guy telling how he stood in front of his nerighbour's burning house, holding a stick with a marshmallow.

The sad thing with these files is they're lacking in variety and often you'll find the same files on different computer, breaking the impression that beyong the machines you're hacking, there are people going about their everyday lives and chatting about different aspects of their lives. As entertaining as they are, once you've read these logs, there's not really anything else worth reading.

Hacknet is pretty linear and all the paths you can take bring you to the same ending. One of the things I found disappointing is, you're never really in much danger, except once, when some other hacked decides to attack you, deleting your UI and forcing you to get out of this mess through terminal. It was a tense moment where I wanted to get back at the guy but none of what I did made the slight difference and once you get out of this mess, there are no other instance where you have to fight off other hackers.

Overall this was a great experience and I would love to play a sequel or at least, an extension, I hope the developper will give us more Hacknet and expand upon all the ideas that were implemented. I wholeheartedly recommend this game for those who like smart, logical experiences and detective games.

Truly amazing game, funny, engaging, and for all types of people who like to solve mysteries and logical puzzles. The story mode can be done under 10 hours, but the game deserves 100% its price.

If you do not have experience in networking, or using computers from command line at all, do not fear. The game introduces you into it gradually and you'll get the trick of it in no time.

If you do (like myself) have experience in networking, or using computers from command line, do not fear either. It feels real, familiar (Unix-like shell), but the "gradually introducing you" is not spoonfeeding you with "type XY to do Z" kind of pop-ups that annoy you. The game has several things "of its own" that you will learn really fast and I saw myself really excited and feeling like I was exploring some kind of distro like BackTrack or Kali Linux and going like "look at the amount of tools we've got!! And they work like a charm, too!"
If you are not a real-life hacker, you'll sure feel like one in here.

I followed the role of a white hat (it aligns with my way of thinking), although some of my in-game actions could qualify enough to be considered "grey". The good thing here is that you have complete freedom to approach and follow the story filling your own role, without the game forcing you into it (or even "presenting" them to you...you have your tools, you decide how to use them and deal with the potential consequences)

The game is full of secrets and jokes to be found here and there (take a look to the IRC logs), the story will keep you immersed from second 0 till the end of it.

Of course the game is not perfect, and I did personally miss some commands, like "cp" (copy files locally), "find" (self explanatory), and some way to create files and edit them beyond using "replace" on them.

I definitely recommend it: 9/10 

PS: Oh, you want some fast tips/hints? Get in fast, do/get what you need to, delete logs (always), get out.
